chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Yahya ibn Hashim, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he traveled a farsakh, would shorten the prayer.

key_terms.قَصَّرَ: shortened (referring to the four-rak'ah prayer reduced to two)

ai.seo_question: At what distance does a traveler shorten their prayers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) consistent practice of shortening prayers after traveling one farsakh, establishing a foundational metric for the distance of travel (masafah) in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the practical application of divine ease, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s Sunnah as the primary source for deriving legal rulings on ritual worship.
